title: Colles fracture: block, reduction and cast
stem: Plaster room. Mrs Wu, 65 (55 kg), fell on her outstretched right hand. Consent has been obtained for closed reduction. You have one assistant and a medical student. Interpret the X-ray, then demonstrate a haematoma block, reduction and cast on the model while teaching the student.

phases.title: Block, reduce and plaster
phases.goal: By hand: check the hand, block the haematoma, reduce, plaster, check again.

phases.title: Advice
phases.goal: Elevation, warning signs, follow-up, bone health.

review.text: Acceptable alignment. Your notes give radial shortening of 5 mm or less, and dorsal angulation of under 5° in one place and under 10° in another. Current thresholds (BOAST, AAOS): shortening 3 mm or less, dorsal tilt 10° or less, intra-articular step 2 mm or less.
Cast. Your notes suggest a long-arm cast first. A moulded below-elbow backslab is standard ED practice for a Colles fracture.

notes:
Checked against BOAST 'Management of distal radial fractures' (2017), AAOS 2020 guideline, and NICE NG38 (non-complex fractures).

Colles: extra-articular distal radius fracture with dorsal angulation, dorsal displacement, radial shortening ('dinner fork'). Check median nerve and EPL (thumb extension) before and after. Anaesthesia: haematoma block (1% lidocaine up to 10 mL, into the fracture haematoma from the dorsum, confirmed by aspirating blood) or Bier's block (IV regional; prilocaine, needs trained staff and a double cuff) or sedation. Reduction: traction with counter-traction to disimpact, then the distal fragment pushed volarly and into ulnar deviation. Below-elbow moulded backslab (three-point moulding); elevate. Repeat X-ray. Acceptable alignment (AAOS/BOAST): radial shortening 3 mm or less, dorsal tilt 10° or less, intra-articular step 2 mm or less; the older patient's function matters more than the film.

Your notes: acceptable radial shortening '5 mm or less' and dorsal angulation '<5°' (in one place) or '<10° dorsally' (in another); current thresholds are 3 mm and 10°. Your notes also suggest a long-arm cast first; a moulded below-elbow backslab is standard in UK/HK ED practice for Colles. The block and sedation steps match.

Perfect script checked against BOAST distal radius and AAOS, an HKCEM-style scheme and a keyword scheme. Spoken bench narration added.

opts.t: Keep it raised and move your fingers; keep the plaster dry. Come back at once for severe pain, numbness or blue fingers. Fracture clinic in 1 week with an X-ray.

script.say: Right wrist PA and lateral. An extra-articular distal radius fracture with dorsal angulation, displacement and radial shortening: a displaced Colles fracture. It needs reducing.
script.do: Extra-articular distal radius fracture 2 cm from the joint with dorsal angulation and displacement, radial shortening; ulnar styloid fracture. "An extra-articular distal radius fracture with dorsal angulation, displacement and radial shortening: a displaced Colles fracture. It needs reducing."

script.say: Check the hand first: median nerve sensation and thumb opposition, EPL thumb extension, circulation and skin. Clean the skin. 1% lidocaine, up to 10 mL, into the radial fracture from the dorsum; aspirate blood to confirm I'm in the haematoma. Wait for the block, and test it. My assistant gives counter-traction at the elbow; I pull to disimpact, then push the distal fragment volar and into ulnar deviation. Backslab on while I hold the reduction, three-point moulding until it sets. Then check the hand again and repeat the X-ray.

Keep it raised and move your fingers; keep the plaster dry. Come back at once for severe pain, numbness or blue fingers. Fracture clinic in 1 week with an X-ray. A wrist fracture from a simple fall can mean thin bones, so we'll arrange a bone health check.
